title: Arthroscopic technique for anterior cruciate ligament repair augmented with an internal brace: Current technique.
abstract: Primary anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) repair serves as a joint-preserving surgical option for carefully selected acute proximal ACL tears (Sherman Type I and II) presenting within 4 weeks of injury. The proximal ACL stump is secured using high-strength FiberWire sutures, which are passed through the adjustable loop of a cortical button incorporating a FiberTape suture that acts as an internal brace. The distal ends of the repair sutures and internal brace tape are subsequently fixed to the proximal anteromedial tibial cortex using an externally attachable button system. Compared with conventional ACL reconstruction, primary repair aims to preserve the native ACL stump and its proprioceptive mechanoreceptors, which may theoretically maintain dynamic stability and physiological knee kinematics while avoiding donor-site morbidity. The internal brace acts as a secondary mechanical stabilizer during the early healing phase, sharing loads to prevent gap formation and protect the biological repair during early motion. This technical note describes patient selection criteria, portal placement, precise construct assembly, differential knee-flexion tensioning, and a criteria-based postoperative rehabilitation protocol.

title: Immediate Effects of Kinesiotaping on Lower Limb Biomechanics and Interlimb Symmetry in Return-to-Sport Athletes After ACL Reconstruction.
abstract: Residual biomechanical deficits may persist during landing after ACL reconstruction despite meeting return-to-sport criteria, and the immediate effects of kinesiotaping (KT) remain unclear. This study investigated bilateral lower limb biomechanics and the immediate effects of KT in 18 return-to-sport athletes after ACL reconstruction. Three-dimensional motion capture and dual force plates were used during the landing absorption phase. Statistical parametric mapping and 2-way repeated-measures analysis of variance were applied for analysis, and the limb symmetry index was calculated to assess interlimb symmetry. The uninvolved limb demonstrated greater vertical ground reaction force, loading rate, knee and ankle joint work (P < .05), hip external rotation moment (P = .025), and knee flexion moment (P < .001) than the involved limb. KT reduced knee varus and external rotation angles and internal knee valgus moment in the involved limb (P < .05) and increased bilateral hip work contribution (P = .026). However, KT did not significantly improve interlimb symmetry (P > .05). ACL reconstruction athletes meeting return-to-sport criteria continue to exhibit bilateral biomechanical asymmetries during landing. KT improved frontal- and transverse-plane knee control and promoted a more proximal energy absorption strategy, but restoring interlimb symmetry requires comprehensive neuromuscular rehabilitation.

title: The Ankle's Roll in Landing: Insights Into ACL Injury Biomechanics.
abstract: Noncontact ACL injuries typically occur within the first 40 milliseconds after ground contact, before voluntary neuromuscular responses can alter joint loading. This study quantified whether early ankle and foot mechanics during single-leg landing are associated with knee biomechanics within an ACL injury-relevant timeframe. Forty-one recreationally active adults performed a horizontal-to-vertical single-leg hop, while kinematics and ground reaction forces were recorded. Gradient-boosted decision tree models with participant-wise leave-one-subject-out cross-validation and nested feature selection were used to predict knee outcomes from ankle mechanics and participant descriptors. Knee-flexion displacement demonstrated the strongest predictive performance (R2 = .430), with greater ankle dorsiflexion at initial contact associated with reduced knee-flexion displacement. Across its interquartile range, initial-contact dorsiflexion was associated with a 4.36° reduction in predicted knee-flexion displacement. Knee-extensor yield impulse demonstrated the next-highest R2 (.334), with greater magnitude early plantarflexor yield impulse associated with greater knee-extensor yield impulse (0.0160 N·m·s·kg-1 across its interquartile range). Frontal-plane knee outcomes and peak vertical ground reaction force were poorly predicted. These findings identify initial-contact ankle-dorsiflexion and early plantarflexor yield impulse as distal variables associated with selected sagittal-plane knee outcomes during early landing.

title: FoRist: Three-DoF Soft Wearable Robot for Forearm and Wrist Assistance.
abstract: The growing population of elderly individuals affected by musculoskeletal and neurological diseases experiences multijoint functional impairment, and individuals with compromised forearm and wrist function can lose independence and quality of life. However, most wearable robotic devices provide assistance for a single degree of freedom (DoF) and restrict other joint movements because decoupling multijoint kinematics remains challenging. This article introduces FoRist, a lightweight three-DoF soft wearable robot designed for forearm and wrist assistance. FoRist assists wrist ulnar/radial deviation, wrist extension/flexion, and forearm pronation/supination through a spring blade-based active-passive hybrid actuation mechanism using three motors. It integrates compact rail structures, soft tension transfer mechanisms, and a flexible twisted string actuation mechanism to assist forearm-wrist motion while preserving freedom of movement in the neighboring hand and elbow joints. The local wearable structure at the wristband rail-slider engagement has a maximum thickness of 16 mm. Its personalized usability features, including bioanatomical analysis-driven customization and user-friendly donning/doffing, support application to individuals with forearm and wrist impairments. User tests with stroke survivors showed that wearing FoRist increased the achievable range of motion and output torque across the forearm and wrist movements compared with unassisted movement. In a two-participant test of a simulated food-preparation sequence involving opening a jar, scooping jam, and spreading jam on bread, FoRist assistance increased task-relevant wrist motion and was associated with lower maximum shoulder abduction. These preliminary results support FoRist's feasibility and usability in short-term laboratory use. With its compact three-DoF architecture, low distal mass, and personalized fit, FoRist offers a promising avenue for extending rehabilitation training beyond clinical settings and has the potential to enhance independence and functional performance in activities of daily living.

title: Hydration-Driven Self-Strengthening Silk Fibroin Ionic Elastomer for Electro-Immunomodulatory Achilles Tendon Repair.
abstract: Achilles tendon repair remains limited by fibrotic healing and implants' inability to coordinate mechanical support, ionic signaling, electrical cues, and immune remodeling in wet load-bearing environments. We report a bioinspired self-strengthening silk fibroin ionic elastomer (SFIE) as an electro-immunomodulatory artificial Achilles tendon. Lithium chloride is integrated into regenerated silk fibroin to create a hydration-responsive protein-ion network. Upon water uptake, LiCl-associated hydration may facilitate chain mobility and the reorganization of hydrophobic silk domains into β-sheet nanocrystals, enhancing tensile strength and modulus while preserving extensibility, fatigue resistance, and ionic conductivity. SFIE sustains Li+ release within a bioactive window that supports bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) viability and tenogenic activity. Mechanistically, SFIE-derived Li+ is associated with altered BMSC paracrine signaling, including reduced arachidonic acid secretion, which may modulate macrophage inflammatory responses. These effects are associated with changes in cPLA2/DUSP3/p38-related signaling. With electrical stimulation, SFIE increases intracellular Ca2 + levels and is associated with changes in CaM/CREB/NR4A1/LIF-related signaling and reduced CXCL10 secretion, potentially contributing to altered macrophage recruitment. In a rat Achilles tendon defect model, SFIE plus electrical stimulation improves gait recovery, tendon continuity, collagen alignment, tendon-marker expression, and local immune remodeling. This work establishes a self-strengthening ionic protein elastomer for functional tendon repair.

title: Scar Treatments in Hand Surgery.
abstract: Scar formation after hand surgery poses unique functional and aesthetic challenges because of the hand's complex anatomy, dense sensory innervation, and reliance on supple skin and tendon glide. Hypertrophic scars, keloids, adherent scars, and contractures can cause pain, hypersensitivity, restricted motion, and impaired activities of daily living, yet evidence guiding scar management in hand surgery remains limited and largely extrapolated from burn and general surgical populations. This review synthesizes current evidence on the biology, classification, prevention, and treatment of scars as they pertain to hand surgery. Nonoperative management, including silicone gel sheeting, compression therapy, intralesional corticosteroid injection, laser therapy, and hand therapy, forms the foundation of care. Operative interventions, ranging from scar excision and Z-plasty to skin grafting, local flap reconstruction, dermal substitutes, and tenolysis, address established contracture and adhesion when conservative measures fail. Emerging therapies, such as autologous fat grafting, growth factor modulation, platelet-rich plasma, and botulinum toxin A, show early promise but require validation in hand-specific trials. Optimal outcomes depend on a collaborative, individualized approach integrating patient risk stratification, meticulous surgical technique, and close coordination with hand therapy throughout the care continuum.

title: Obturator internus muscle entrapment in posterior wall acetabular fractures: two cases with preoperative and intraoperative findings.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: We report two cases of the rare presentation of obturator internus muscle (OI) entrapment in posterior wall fractures of the acetabulum. Although piriformis muscle entrapment has been previously reported, to the best of our knowledge, OI entrapment associated with posterior wall acetabular fractures has not been previously documented.
CASE PRESENTATION: Case 1: A 38-year-old male presented with right hip and knee pain following a road traffic accident. He was diagnosed with a posterior hip dislocation, posterior wall and posterior column fractures of the acetabulum, and a posterior knee dislocation. During surgery, the OI muscle was found interposed between the displaced posterior wall fragment and the remaining posterior column. Case 2: A 43-year-old male sustained blunt abdominal trauma and a Pipkin type IV injury involving a femoral head fracture associated with a posterior wall acetabular fracture following a road traffic accident. After stabilisation of the abdominal injury with laparoscopic repair of the mesenteric injury, the patient underwent open reduction and internal fixation of the posterior wall fracture, along with removal of intra-articular fragments associated with an infra-foveal femoral head fracture. Intraoperatively, the OI muscle was similarly found interposed between the displaced posterior wall fragment and the remaining posterior column. In both cases, retrospective review of the preoperative CT images demonstrated OI interposition corresponding to the intraoperative findings. Both patients followed a standard postoperative rehabilitation protocol. At the one-year follow-up, both patients had satisfactory clinical outcomes, with Merle d'Aubigné-Postel scores of 16 and 17 and Harris Hip Scores of 92.7 and 93 for Cases 1 and 2, respectively. Neither patient showed radiographic evidence of post-traumatic arthritis.
CONCLUSION: These cases highlight the importance of recognising OI muscle entrapment as a potential cause of difficulty in reducing posterior wall acetabular fractures. Careful evaluation of preoperative CT images, particularly using soft-tissue window settings, may facilitate the identification of OI interposition. Intraoperatively, failure to identify the OI tendon between the superior and inferior gemelli, when both are clearly identified, should raise suspicion of entrapment. Meticulous identification of soft-tissue structures may help achieve anatomical fracture reduction and successful fixation.

title: Design and Repeatability Testing of a Novel Benchtop Apparatus for Evaluating Wear Durability of Artificial Tendons.
abstract: Artificial tendons are potential alternatives to biological grafts for reconstructing large tendon defects, yet their clinical translation is limited partly by mechanical durability during repetitive gliding against pulley-like structures (e.g., retinacula). Standardized methods for evaluating long-term tendon-pulley wear under physiologically relevant conditions are lacking. This study aimed to develop a benchtop testing methodology for mechanical wear of artificial tendons after high-cycle loading. A custom apparatus was designed to simulate key biomechanical features of the flexor pollicis longus tendon, including tensile load, excursion velocity, and wrapping angle at the tendon-pulley interface. Apparatus performance and repeatability were evaluated using polyester tendons subjected to 1.02 million simulated thumb flexions, equivalent to approximately 395 days of simulated physiological thumb motion, at a rate of 22.1 simulated flexions per second. Non-lubricated testing resulted in excessive frictional heating (93 °C within 40,800 simulated thumb flexions), causing premature thermal damage and ultimate tensile strength (UTS) variability. Conversely, applying boundary lubricant at the tendon-pulley interface, mimicking synovial fluid, maintained temperatures at approximately 36 °C and eliminated non-physiological thermal degradation. Under lubricated conditions, wear scar morphology was consistent with isolated mechanical fiber abrasion, and median UTS was 865.7 N (848.0-887.2 N), with high inter-trial repeatability across three independent tests (p = 0.3688). This study establishes a reproducible experimental framework for isolating mechanical wear in artificial tendons under high-cycle gliding and is suited for orthopaedic research applications, including material screening and design optimization of tendon grafts and tendon-implant interfaces.

title: Immediate effect of verbal cues on ACL injury relevant Knee loading during 180° and 90° cutting maneuvers in female university soccer and basketball athletes.
abstract: Young female athletes possess a high risk of rupturing their anterior cruciate ligament (ACL). High external peak knee abduction moments (pKAM) are a likely key risk factor for non-contact ACL injuries. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of performance-based movement feedback on pKAM during cutting maneuvers in female university athletes. Thirty-four female university soccer and basketball athletes completed preplanned 180° and 90° cutting trials while ground reaction forces and kinematics were simultaneously captured. Participants immediately received verbal cues targeting foot strike angle, foot progression angle, or trunk lean angle based on their performance. Athletes then repeated the trials post-feedback. Changes in pKAM between baseline and post-feedback trials were analyzed. Soccer and basketball athletes who received the FOOTstrike-angle cue significantly reduced pKAM for both cutting tasks (Soccer: 180°; -0.21 Nm/kg, p < 0.01, d = 0.92; 90°; -0.28 Nm/kg, p < 0.01, d = 1.16. Basketball: 180°; -0.07 Nm/kg, p = 0.02, d = 0.76; 90°; -0.30 Nm/kg, p < 0.01, d = 0.82). The FOOTpro-angle cue significantly reduced pKAM during the 180° cut for soccer athletes (-0.10 Nm/kg, p = 0.01, d = 0.60), but not basketball. The TRUNKlean cue did not significantly affect pKAM for either sport. Individual feedback targeting forefoot landings and neutral foot progression angles can elicit immediate technique change and reduce ACL injury relevant knee loading during cutting maneuvers.

title: Sexual dimorphism in morphological predictors of upper- and lower-limb strength in adult rugby players.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex differences in athletic performance extend beyond body size, encompassing morphology-strength relationships.
AIM: To analyse sex-specific associations between body size and composition (body mass, fat-free mass [FFM], and thigh volume) and strength (hand grip strength and isokinetic knee extensor and flexor strength) in adult rugby players.
SUBJECTS AND METHODS: 84 players (42 males) were assessed. Body composition was measured by air-displacement plethysmography, and thigh volume was estimated anthropometrically. Strength was measured by grip (kg) and isokinetic knee torque at 60°·s-1.
RESULTS: Males were taller (178.3 cm), heavier (82.7 kg), and stronger (hand grip: 48.2 kg; knee extensors: 252 N·m). Females had a higher fat percentage (24.2% vs. 14.1%) and lower strength. FFM was the best predictor of peak torque in males (r ≈ 0.69 to 0.74); body mass correlated best (r ≈ 0.45 to 0.50) with peak torque in females. The hamstring-to-quadriceps ratio was, on average, 0.56 in both sexes.
CONCLUSION: Strength determinants differ by sex in rugby players. FFM is the primary predictor of strength in males, whereas body mass is more relevant in females. These findings support the development of sex-specific training methods to optimise performance and potentially reduce injury risk.

title: Combined Arthroscopic Hip Correction and Open Core Muscle Repair for Concomitant Femoroacetabular Impingement and Athletic Pubalgia: A Surgical Technique.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Concomitant femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) and core muscle injury (athletic pubalgia) represent an increasingly recognized source of persistent hip and groin pain in young athletes, with up to 94% of professional athletes with symptomatic FAI demonstrating signs of athletic pubalgia. Biomechanical alterations from FAI-particularly restricted hip internal rotation and compensatory pelvic mechanics-may predispose athletes to core muscle pathology. Isolated treatment yields suboptimal outcomes, with return-to-sport rates of 25% to 50% when only 1 pathology is addressed. We present the surgical technique for concurrent open core muscle repair and hip arthroscopy in a high-level athlete.
TECHNIQUE DESCRIPTION: The procedure is performed in 2 stages under a single anesthetic. Core muscle repair is performed first with the patient supine. A standard inguinal incision identifies external oblique fascial pathology. Full-thickness adductor longus tenotomy is performed at the pubic insertion. Ilioinguinal neurectomy is completed, followed by rectus muscle lateralization and reinforcement using interrupted permanent sutures to the pubic tubercle and iliopubic tract. After fascial closure, the patient is repositioned for hip arthroscopy, with standard anterolateral and mid-anterior portals, labral repair, femoroplasty for cam correction, and complete capsular closure.
RESULTS: Combined management of FAI and athletic pubalgia demonstrates superior outcomes compared with isolated treatment, with return-to-sport rates of 89% to 100% when both pathologies are addressed versus 25% to 50% for single-pathology treatment. All patient-reported outcome measures improve significantly after combined procedures. While treating FAI alone may successfully manage dual pathology in select patients, those with prominent core symptoms and imaging findings typically require formal core repair for optimal results.
CONCLUSION: In competitive athletes with persistent hip and groin pain, failure to recognize and address concomitant FAI and core muscle injury leads to incomplete symptom resolution and compromised performance. A biomechanical assessment revealing restricted hip internal rotation combined with core tenderness and pubic bone edema on magnetic resonance imaging should prompt evaluation for dual pathology. Combined surgical treatment under a single anesthetic represents a single-stage approach that optimizes outcomes and facilitates full return to competitive athletics in appropriately selected patients.

title: The Mechanical Regulatory Window of Cartilage Metabolism in Knee Osteoarthritis: From Mechanosensation to Parameter-Based Intervention Design.
abstract: Mechanical loading occupies a paradoxical position in osteoarthritis (OA): it contributes to cartilage degeneration, yet exercise is an established component of conservative OA care. This review advances the concept of a mechanical regulatory window of cartilage metabolism, a hypothesis-generating framework relating the magnitude, frequency, duration and mode of mechanical signals to chondrocyte metabolic responses. We synthesize evidence from the chondrocyte mechanosensory apparatus: ion channels and hemichannels, integrin-mediated adhesion, primary cilium-dependent signaling, and the pericellular matrix, to examine how their engagement under different loading conditions influences matrix homeostasis and catabolism. TRPV4 and PIEZO1/2 have context-dependent functions; inflammatory mediators can alter channel expression and amplify deformation-associated cellular injury. The window position may vary with disease state, inflammatory milieu, pericellular matrix properties and loading history. Tensile strain, construct compression, single-cell compression and substrate stiffness describe different physical inputs, and their numerical values cannot define a shared loading threshold. We identify three barriers to clinical translation: limited measurement of chondrocyte-level mechanical signals during treatment, incomplete mapping of mechanosensory signaling, and inconsistent parameter reporting across mechanical intervention studies. Addressing these gaps could support the rational design of mechanical interventions for OA. The proposed window remains to be validated against sustained cartilage and patient outcomes.

title: The Over-the-Top Technique Promotes Early Femoral Tendon-Soft Tissue Healing and Tibial Tendon-Bone Integration: An Experimental Study in Rabbits.
abstract: This study compared femoral graft healing and inflammatory responses following over-the-top (OTT) versus anatomical single-bundle (ASB) ACL reconstruction in 40 rabbits. Evaluations at 4, 8, and 12 weeks utilized histology, immunohistochemistry, ELISA, and biomechanical testing. Results showed OTT reconstruction, avoiding femoral tunnels, healed via tendon-soft tissue integration with dense fibrous connections by 4-8 weeks. Conversely, ASB healing occurred within tunnels, developing a classic four-layer enthesis by week 12. Type II collagen was significantly higher in OTT at week 4 but lower at week 8 (P<0.05). OTT grafts exhibited less edema and significantly lower synovial MMP-13 at week 4 (P<0.05). Biomechanically, OTT demonstrated superior maximum failure load at week 4 (65.5 N vs. 56.8 N, P=0.04), converging with ASB by week 12. Consequently, OTT reconstruction offers faster early integration, superior initial strength, and reduced early inflammation compared to the slower, classical enthesis pathway of ASB. These findings clarify OTT's distinct healing mechanism, supporting its clinical application for early rehabilitation, though clinical validation remains necessary.

title: Hydrogels as drug carriers for cartilage repair in osteoarthritis: Applications and challenges.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent chronic degenerative joint disease characterized by progressive cartilage degradation, subchondral bone remodelling, synovial inflammation, osteophyte formation, and loss of joint function, resulting in significant pain, disability, and socioeconomic burden worldwide. Despite advances in clinical management, current therapeutic strategies, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, corticosteroids, hyaluronic acid injections, and surgical interventions, primarily provide symptomatic relief and have limited ability to prevent disease progression or regenerate damaged cartilage. In recent years, hydrogel-based drug delivery systems have emerged as promising therapeutic platforms owing to their excellent biocompatibility, biodegradability, injectability, high water content, and structural similarity to the native extracellular matrix. These properties enable hydrogels to serve as effective carriers for a wide range of therapeutic agents, including anti-inflammatory drugs, growth factors, nucleic acids, nanoparticles, exosomes, and stem cells, while providing sustained and localized drug release within the osteoarthritic joint. This review comprehensively discusses the pathophysiology of OA and highlights the major molecular signaling pathways involved in disease progression, including NF-κB, MAPK, Wnt/β-catenin, PI3K/Akt, TGF-β, and JAK/STAT pathways. Furthermore, recent advances in natural, synthetic, hybrid, and stimuli-responsive hydrogels are critically examined, with particular emphasis on their applications in cartilage repair and targeted drug delivery. Emerging approaches involving nanotechnology-enabled hydrogels, gene delivery systems, stem cell-loaded constructs, and immunomodulatory biomaterials are also evaluated for their therapeutic potential and translational prospects. This review provides an integrated and up-to-date perspective on hydrogel-based strategies for cartilage regeneration and disease modification, highlighting their potential as next-generation therapeutic platforms for the long-term management of osteoarthritis.

title: Post-Exercise Thermal Interventions and Nocturnal Sleep in Athletes: A Narrative Review of the Potential Underlying Physiological Mechanisms.
abstract: Sleep is essential for optimal performance and recovery in athletes. Post-exercise cold exposure, including cold water immersion and cryotherapy, is typically used to enhance recovery, but its effects on sleep remain unclear. Emerging evidence also suggests that post-exercise heat exposure, including sauna and hot water immersion before sleep may improve both objective and subjective sleep outcomes. However, the effectiveness of post-exercise thermal interventions for improving nocturnal sleep in athletes specifically has not yet been comprehensively evaluated. This narrative review synthesizes the current evidence and discusses the potential physiological mechanisms by which post-exercise thermal interventions may influence nocturnal sleep in athletes. Despite methodological heterogeneity, existing research indicates that post-exercise thermal interventions may influence the subsequent nocturnal sleep of athletes through multiple and varying interacting mechanisms. For example, cold exposure close to bedtime (< 2 h) may disrupt sleep by reducing the distal-to-proximal skin temperature gradient (DPG), thereby increasing sleep onset latency and shortening sleep duration. In contrast, when applied more than 2 h before bedtime, cold exposure may improve sleep by augmenting parasympathetic tone and/or reducing muscle soreness and associated nocturnal movement. Although it remains unclear whether post-exercise heat exposure improves sleep via autonomic modulation or reduced muscle soreness, existing evidence indicates that sleep may be facilitated by an increased DPG. Moderating factors such as sex, time of day, environmental temperature, bedding microclimate, acclimatization status, and training load may influence the effects of post-exercise thermal interventions on sleep and should be investigated in future studies.

title: Subject-Specific Cardiovascular Signatures Revealed by Arterial Pulse Signals in Patients with Heart Diseases-Part I: General Cases.
abstract: Background/Objectives: This study evaluates whether cardiovascular (CV) parameters derived from noninvasive arterial pulse signals can capture subject-specific physiological characteristics and longitudinal changes in patients with diverse heart diseases. Method: Arterial pulse signals at the radial artery (RA) and carotid artery (CA) of each patient were successfully recorded from all 18 patients using micro-fabricated tactile sensors. Signal quality was screened before analysis, and the accepted signals were analyzed using a single-degree-of-freedom time-frequency (SDOF-TF) framework. Key CV parameters, including time-based indices-heart rate (HR), heart rate variability (HRV), respiration rate (RR), and respiration modulation (RM), as well as harmonic amplitudes and normalized arterial pulse waveform (APW)-were extracted from measurements at rest and post-exercise across three rehabilitation visits in 18 patients with heterogeneous CV conditions. Longitudinal changes in CV parameters within subjects and variability between subjects were assessed. Results: Compared with a healthy reference, the patients exhibited heterogeneous CV profiles, with lower HRV in all patients except one with AF, who showed elevated HRV, and generally reduced post-exercise CV responses. Higher-order harmonic amplitudes were attenuated at the RA, while CA-derived APW measurements showed greater sensitivity to systolic upstroke slope. Marked inter-subject variability was evident in at-rest CV parameters and 5-min post-exercise responses. Longitudinal CV responses varied across rehabilitation visits, potentially reflecting multiple contributing factors. Conclusions: The 100% pulse acquisition rate supports the feasibility of the tactile sensor technology for pulse measurement, and the combined sensor technology and SDOF-TF framework enable quantitative characterization of shared and individualized CV patterns in cardiac patients and their post-exercise recovery, including time-based indices, harmonic signatures, site-specific differences, and interactions among CV parameters. These findings warrant further investigation in larger cohorts with appropriate physiological reference measurements.

title: The impact of mindfulness on sleep, cognitive function and athletic performance of young males migrating to the plateau.
abstract:
AIMS: To examine whether an 8-week mindfulness training program was associated with changes in sleep quality, cognitive function, and athletic performance in young men who migrated to high-altitude regions.
METHODS: Ninety-six young male migrants were randomly assigned to an 8-week mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT) program (n = 48) or a no-intervention control group (n = 48). Sleep quality (PSQI), cognitive processing (P300 latency), and athletic performance (3000-m run time) were assessed before and after the intervention.
RESULTS: The mindfulness group was associated with greater improvements in sleep quality (PSQI median: 7.5 to 5 vs. 8 to 8.5, P < 0.001) and cognitive processing speed (P300 latency median: 387 ms to 357 ms vs. 376.5 ms to 374.5 ms, P = 0.01) compared with controls. Exploratory analyses suggested that P300 amplitude increased in parietal and occipital regions. No significant between-group difference was observed in 3000-m run completion time (P = 0.51) or grade improvement rates (25.0% vs. 29.17%, P = 0.65).
CONCLUSION: An 8-week mindfulness intervention was associated with improved sleep quality and cognitive processing speed, but no significant association was observed with athletic performance, in young male migrants to high-altitude regions. These preliminary findings suggest potential benefits of mindfulness as a non-pharmacological strategy for high-altitude health management, pending replication with active control conditions.

title: Sex- and Sport-Specific Differences in Mobility and Muscle Function Characteristics in Division I Athletes.
abstract: Gonzalez, AM, Sell, KM, Mangine, GT, Ghigiarelli, JJ, Gerland, RW, Deveaux, B, DiMonda, R, Prendergast, JM, and Bentivegna, J. Sex- and sport-specific differences in mobility and muscle function characteristics in Division I athletes. J Strength Cond Res 40(12): 1569-1580, 2026-The purpose of the present investigation was to compare sex- and sport-specific differences in joint mobility, bilateral asymmetry, and muscle function characteristics among Division I collegiate athletes. Two hundred and seventy six male (n = 144) and female (n = 132) athletes from 7 sports completed a comprehensive, preseason assessment battery. Mobility assessments included hip, shoulder, ankle, thoracic, and pelvic range-of-motion, as well as sit-and-reach performance. Muscle function assessments included measures of vertical jump height, hand grip strength, and hip abduction/adduction strength. Measures were analyzed using mixed-model analyses of variance to examine effects of sex, sport, and limb dominance. Clear sex- and sport-specific differences were observed across multiple mobility measures. Female athletes demonstrated significantly greater joint mobility than male athletes across several anatomical regions (p < 0.001-0.03; η2p = 0.02-0.16), whereas male athletes display superior muscle function performance across strength (p < 0.001-0.02; η2p = 0.06-0.3) and vertical jump (p < 0.001, η2p = 0.50) measures. Mobility asymmetries varied substantially by sport and joint, while strength asymmetries were minimal across groups. These findings provide sex- and sport-specific reference data and reinforce the importance of individualized interpretation of mobility and muscle function assessments in athletic populations.

title: Changes in energy availability, nutritional status, and physiological health across training phases in elite Chinese artistic swimmers.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low energy availability (LEA) adversely affects athletes'physiological health, yet studies in elite synchronized swimmers across different pre-competition training phases are scarce. This study evaluated changes in energy availability, nutritional status, and physiological health in Chinese elite female synchronized swimmers before the National Games.
METHODS: Ten Chinese elite female synchronized swimmers sequentially completed a 1-week tapering phase (TP) and a 4-week intensified training phase (ITP). At the end of each phase, dietary intake (weighed food records), exercise energy expenditure (heart rate monitoring), energy availability (EA), resting metabolic rate (RMR), body composition, and blood biomarkers were measured. Within each training phase, athletes were classified into LEA and non-LEA groups according to their EA levels, and between-group differences were compared. In addition, overall changes between TP and ITP were analyzed in the full cohort of 10 athletes.
RESULTS: LEA prevalence was 40% during the TP and 60% during the ITP. In unadjusted analyzes, the LEA group showed significantly lower EI (p = 0.025), VO₂ (p = 0.022), mRMR (p = 0.023), RMR ratio (p = 0.006), and intakes of carbohydrate (p = 0.023), protein (p = 0.015), fat (p = 0.032), calcium (p = 0.038), and iron (p = 0.044) during the TP, with large effect-size estimates. As expected from the classification criteria, EA was significantly lower in the LEA group during both the TP (p = 0.001) and ITP (p = 0.005). During the ITP, fat (p = 0.027) and zinc intakes (p = 0.036) were significantly lower in the LEA group, whereas carbohydrate and protein intakes were lower but did not reach statistical significance. In the overall cohort, EEE (p < 0.001) and T4 (p = 0.010) increased from TP to ITP, whereas ferritin (p = 0.012) and calcium intake (p = 0.007) decreased, with large effect-size estimates.
CONCLUSION: During intensified training, EEE increased without a corresponding increase in EI, suggesting that dietary intake may not have adequately matched the increased training demands and may have increased susceptibility to LEA. LEA was associated with lower energy and macronutrient intakes, potential calcium and iron inadequacies, and phase-specific reductions in RMR-related measures. Phase-related biomarker changes could not be attributed specifically to LEA. Individualized and periodized nutritional monitoring and intervention are recommended to better align energy and nutrient intake with training demands and support athlete health and performance.

title: Dysphagia as the Initial Manifestation of Anti-HMGCR Antibody-Positive Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy Complicated by Pulmonary Embolism.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anti-3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (anti-HMGCR) antibody-positive immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) is a rare autoimmune myopathy characterized by progressive proximal muscle weakness and markedly elevated creatine kinase levels. Although commonly associated with prior statin exposure, statin-naïve cases and atypical presentations are well described. Patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies are also at increased risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE), though data specific to IMNM remain limited.
CASE PRESENTATION: An 83-year-old man with brief, remote statin exposure presented with progressive proximal muscle weakness and a three-year history of oropharyngeal dysphagia preceding limb involvement. Laboratory evaluation revealed markedly elevated creatine kinase and transaminases. Anti-HMGCR antibodies were positive, and muscle biopsy confirmed necrotizing myopathy. During evaluation for occult malignancy, bilateral pulmonary emboli were incidentally identified. The patient required high-dose corticosteroids, mycophenolate mofetil, and intravenous immunoglobulin for refractory disease. With aggressive immunosuppressive therapy and rehabilitation, he demonstrated substantial clinical recovery at 6 months.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights oropharyngeal dysphagia as an early and, for a prolonged period, isolated manifestation of anti-HMGCR antibody-positive IMNM; here, it preceded the onset of limb weakness by approximately 3 years. It underscores the importance of comprehensive diagnostic evaluation in patients with unexplained oropharyngeal dysfunction, in whom an inflammatory myopathy may otherwise be overlooked for years. Clinicians should maintain awareness of thrombotic risk in inflammatory myopathies, particularly during active disease. Early recognition and prompt immunosuppressive therapy remain critical to optimize outcomes and prevent irreversible muscle damage.

title: Vertical jump landing kinetics may be more sensitive to delayed-onset muscle soreness effects than forward and drop jumps.
abstract: Exercise-induced delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS) may reduce joint range of motion and transiently impair muscle strength. However, DOMS-related symptoms do not consistently translate into measurable biomechanical changes in landing mechanics. Here we set out to determine whether exercise-induced DOMS alters landing kinetics in different landing tasks. Twenty-six physically active adults (15 women and 11 men) completed a squat protocol to induce lower extremity DOMS. Before and 48 h after the protocol, DOMS was assessed using a numerical pain rating scale, and the landing kinetics data were recorded during forward, vertical, and drop jumps. Joint stiffness and the joint contributions to the total support moment were determined and compared between baseline and DOMS conditions. DOMS significantly increased perceived muscle soreness and reduced vertical jump height by 16%. Joint stiffness did not differ between baseline and DOMS conditions for any landing task. Changes in total support moment (TSM) distribution were observed during vertical jump landings, with a reduced relative hip contribution at initial contact and an increased relative knee contribution at maximum knee flexion. No significant changes in TSM distribution were observed during forward or drop jump landings. These findings indicate that lower extremity DOMS may not necessarily alter overall landing stiffness but can modify inter-joint movement and torque strategies in vertical jump landing, highlighting the importance of evaluating movement mechanics alongside performance measures during recovery from strenuous exercise.

title: Genicular Artery Embolization for Knee Osteoarthritis: A Practical Guide and Future Directions on behalf of French Society of Rheumatology, Musculoskeletal Imaging Society, French Hip and Knee Society, French Society for Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery, French Society of Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine, and of French Society of Radiology.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To establish considerations for the indication and performance of genicular arteries embolization (GAE) for painful knee osteoarthritis on behalf of consortium of national societies.
METHODS: Based on literature review and clinical practice, a multidisciplinary group of 16 healthcare professionals including rheumatologists, interventional and MSK radiologists, physical and rehabilitation medicine physicians, knee orthopedic surgeons, and member of people living with OA association produced the considerations. Results : The group established 11 specific considerations. GAE is indicated for patients with painful knee osteoarthritis for whom no other cause of pain can be identified, and whose pain is refractory despite usual optimal medical treatment. A pre-therapeutic knee synovitis should be searched prior to GAE using a Doppler ultrasound or, even better, a contrast-enhanced MRI. Interventional radiologists should perform pre- and post-GAE consultations in collaboration with other musculoskeletal physician, in order to integrate GAE into the multimodal management strategy. Currently, there is no consensus on GAE techniques, and these should be individualized according to patient characteristics and interventional radiologist preferences. GAE may be repeated in selected cases. There are no contraindications to undergoing knee surgery after having GAE, but after a reasonable delay of three months. GAE may be considered in selected patients with persistent knee pain after knee replacement and after exclusion of other causes, including joint infection.
CONCLUSIONS: These considerations provide a structured guide for GAE in painful knee osteoarthritis. Several questions warrant further investigation through clinical or basic research.

title: Open Extensor Carpi Radialis Brevis Debridement Augmented by Bioinductive Collagen Implant: Indications and Surgical Technique.
abstract: Lateral epicondylitis is a common cause of elbow pain that typically resolves with conservative management. For patients with persistent symptoms and failed nonoperative treatment, surgical intervention may be considered. We describe a surgical technique for open extensor carpi radialis brevis debridement with augmentation using a bovine-derived bioinductive collagen implant. The procedure involves direct visualization and excision of degenerative tendon, followed by extensor carpi radialis longus tendon repair using a suture anchor. A bioinductive patch is secured over the repair using absorbable staples and suture. This technique builds on principles established in rotator cuff repair, where bioinductive implants have shown increased tendon thickness, organized tissue regeneration, and reduced retear rates. Although no studies currently assess the efficacy of collagen augmentation in lateral epicondylitis, its hypothesized benefit lies in enhancing tendon healing and promoting growth of new tissue after debridement. Contraindications include active infection and allergy to implant materials. Postoperative rehabilitation includes early range of motion and gradual strengthening. This technique provides a reproducible approach to augment open extensor carpi radialis brevis debridement and warrants further studies to evaluate the effect of bioinductive patch augmentation and outcomes in patients with recalcitrant lateral epicondylitis.

title: Intermediate Densification of Collagen Hydrogels Promotes Fibrocartilage-Like Tendon-Bone Healing.
abstract: Regeneration of the fibrocartilaginous tendon-bone enthesis remains a challenge because scar tissue often replaces the functional transitional interface. Biomaterial scaffolds can provide physical cues for interface regeneration, but conventional collagen hydrogels have sparse fibrillar networks and low stiffness. Here, graded plastic compression co-tuned collagen density, pore area fraction, degradation behavior, and multiscale stiffness within a chemically unchanged collagen I system. The target reductions in initial gel thickness were 0% (non-compressed, NC), 50% (low-compression, LC), 70% (moderate-compression, MC), and 90% (high-compression, HC). Material properties changed progressively across these conditions, whereas bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) responses were non-monotonic. MC was the first condition to show a marked increase in bulk stiffness, with corresponding local stiffening, while remaining less compact than HC; it also produced the most favorable overall proliferation, fibrocartilage-associated marker expression, and matrix deposition among the four conditions tested. RNA sequencing revealed MC-associated transcriptional programs related to the cell cycle, cartilage development, extracellular matrix organization, and candidate mechanosensing processes. Pharmacological FAK inhibition reduced MC-associated FAK phosphorylation, YAP1 nuclear localization, and SOX9 expression without a measurable change in total integrin β1 fluorescence intensity, supporting a FAK-sensitive contribution within the YAP1/SOX9 response. In a rat rotator cuff repair model, the selected MC construct improved gait and mechanical properties and promoted more organized fibrocartilage-like interface remodeling compared with the control conditions. These findings identify an intermediate densification physical window within the tested collagen I series and establish graded compression as a practical strategy for selecting collagen constructs for tendon-bone repair. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Rotator cuff repair rarely restores the fibrocartilaginous tendon-bone interface. Existing biomaterial studies often vary scaffold composition, bioactive signals, and physical properties together, making the contribution of matrix physical state difficult to define. By applying graded plastic compression to a compositionally constant type I collagen system, this study identifies an intermediate densification window that outperforms both minimally and maximally compressed matrices in supporting mesenchymal stem cell proliferation and fibrocartilage-associated differentiation. Transcriptomic profiling and pharmacological inhibition further support a FAK-sensitive contribution to the YAP1/SOX9 response. The selected construct also improves gait, mechanical properties, and interface organization in vivo. These findings reveal a non-monotonic structure-function relationship and provide a broadly relevant physical design principle for regenerative biomaterials and tendon-bone repair.

title: Heterotopic ossification: a comprehensive narrative review of pathophysiology, diagnosis, prevention, and emerging therapies.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heterotopic ossification is the formation of mature bone in extraskeletal soft tissues after trauma, orthopaedic surgery, burns, or neurological injury.
REVIEW FINDINGS: Pathogenesis involves mesenchymal stem cell differentiation driven by bone morphogenetic protein, transforming growth factor beta, Wnt/beta-catenin, and hypoxia-inducible factor signalling within an inflammatory microenvironment. Ultrasound detects the zone phenomenon approximately two weeks before radiography; magnetic resonance imaging shows striate and checkerboard patterns in pre-calcification lesions. Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and low-dose radiation remain effective prophylactic strategies. Physiotherapy is central to conservative management, and extracorporeal shock wave therapy may benefit traumatic cases. Excision is reserved for symptomatic lesions causing significant functional limitation, pain, or neurovascular compromise, ideally after maturation to reduce recurrence, although earlier intervention may be feasible in selected athletes.
CONCLUSION: Palovarotene is the first disease-modifying treatment approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva. An individualised, multidisciplinary approach is essential; biomarker research and targeted pharmacotherapy remain priorities.

title: Therapeutic potential of umbilical cord-derived MSCs in arthritis: Insights from preclinical and clinical studies.
abstract: Among different types of arthritis, osteoarthritis (OA) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remain the most common and primary cause of pain and disability worldwide, characterized by progressive joint degeneration and persistent inflammation. Although there have been developments in pharmacology, the available treatment program slows disease progression and provides only symptomatic relief. However, their ability to repair and restore damaged tissue is limited. This highlights the importance of regenerative therapy in actively modulating the immune system while stimulating tissue regeneration. We conducted a narrative review of PubMed, Scopus, Web of science, ClinicalTrials.gov, and ChiCTR, focusing on preclinical and clinical studies of umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells (UC-MSCs) therapy in OA and RA. Recently, UC-MSC have been emerging as a promising therapeutic approach due to their immunomodulatory and regenerative properties. Because they are harvested noninvasively, these cells have greater proliferative capacity and lower immunogenicity than MSCs derived from bone marrow or adipose tissue. UC-MSCs do not replace damaged cells; instead, they signal other cells to produce bioactive substances that reduce inflammation and promote cartilage repair. Data from emerging preclinical and clinical trials, which show significant improvements in WOMAC and VAS scores and a decrease in DAS28 with minimal adverse effects, suggest that UC-MSCs will improve pain and function and, in turn, overall quality of life. UC-MSCs represent a mechanistically distinct and clinically promising therapeutic effect for OA and RA, addressing both the inflammatory and degenerative condition of joint disease. However, there are still large, well-designed, standardized clinical trials that can best optimize doses and treatment plans. This narrative review summarizes the various forms of arthritis, disease pathogenesis, and preclinical and clinical evidence for the use of UC-MSCs in the treatment of arthritis, such as OA and RA.

title: Arthroscopic Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Using Iliotibial Band Autograft With Bone Block.
abstract: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction is the first-line treatment for ACL injury, whereas existing autologous grafts each have inherent limitations. This study describes the use of an iliotibial band (ITB) graft with a bone block for ACL reconstruction, designed as a femoral bone block combined with tibial tendon configuration, which precisely matches the anatomical attachment and biomechanical loading characteristics of the native ACL. The surgery is performed through arthroscopic evaluation, harvesting and weaving of the ITB with a bone block, creation of femoral and tibial bone tunnels, and graft introduction and fixation. This graft features the advantage of easy harvesting of the ITB, whereas the femoral bone column allows for rapid bone-to-bone healing, enhances stability within the femoral tunnel, and reduces the risk of tunnel widening and femoral-sided rerupture. Tibial-sided tendon fixation avoids excessive tibial tunnel enlargement and simplifies surgical steps. Arthroscopic ACL reconstruction using the ITB with bone block is technically straightforward and provides high initial stability. It offers another graft option for both primary treatment of ACL injury and revision surgery after failed reconstructions and is particularly suitable for patients with multiple previous tendon harvests from the same knee or those requiring large-diameter grafts because of bone tunnel enlargement.

title: Temporal coupling shapes the effects of prolonged muscle-tendon vibration on sensorimotor EEG activity during motor imagery.
abstract: Motor imagery (MI) recruits sensorimotor networks overlapping those engaged during physical execution and represents a promising rehabilitation tool. While concurrent afferent stimulation enhances MI-related cortical engagement, the effects of prolonged proprioceptive conditioning prior to MI remain unexplored. This study investigated whether prolonged muscle-tendon vibration (MTV) could modulate cortical activity during subsequent MI, indexed by electroencephalographic alpha- and beta-band event-related desynchronization (ERD). Twenty healthy adults performed imagined maximal isometric knee extensions before and after 20-minute suprapatellar MTV (100 Hz) or SHAM vibration (30 Hz with foam interface) in counterbalanced sessions. Cortical engagement was assessed via EEG burst detection over central electrodes (C3, Cz, C4). Maximal force capacity, submaximal force estimation performance, and cortical responses during combined MI and MTV were also evaluated. MTV induced stronger vibratory responses than SHAM, consistent with enhanced proprioceptive afferent activation. Following MTV, voluntary force outcomes showed near-threshold changes consistent with the expected direction, namely reduced maximal force capacity and altered submaximal force calibration, suggesting modified proprioceptive feedback. MI performed after MTV conditioning exhibited reduced alpha- and beta-band ERD compared to SHAM, with greater vibratory-induced responses being associated with a less pronounced post-vibration beta ERD. Conversely, when MI was performed concurrently with MTV following conditioning, alpha-band ERD increased selectively in the MTV session, with no modulation in the beta band. These findings suggest that prolonged proprioceptive conditioning modulates MI-related cortical engagement differently depending on the sensorimotor context in which imagery is performed. Such state-dependent effects may support distinct intervention strategies aimed either at recalibrating maladaptive sensorimotor patterns or at enhancing cortical recruitment in rehabilitation contexts.

title: Nationwide Trends, Regional Variation and Seasonality of Surgically Treated Achilles Tendon Rupture in Japan: An Analysis of Descriptive Epidemiological Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Achilles tendon rupture (ATR) is a common foot and ankle injury among physically active adults. Nationwide evidence on long-term trends, regional variation, seasonality and COVID-19-related changes in Japan is limited. We characterised the surgical burden of ATR using a national administrative database.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide descriptive epidemiological study using aggregated data from the National Database of Health Insurance Claims and Specific Health Checkups (NDB) Open Data for fiscal years (FY) 2014-2022. Temporal trends, prefectural variation, seasonal patterns and pandemic-associated changes were examined using counts, population-based rates and quasi-Poisson regression.
RESULTS: During FY2014-2019, approximately 11,200 surgeries were performed annually (8.8 per 100,000 person). In FY2020, incidence declined to 5.9 per 100,000 (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0.67), with greater reductions among adults aged 30-59 (61%-64% of baseline) and, after age adjustment, among women (IRR 0.61 vs. 0.71 in men; interaction p = 0.039). Incidence partially recovered in FY2021-2022 (7.6 per 100,000; IRR 0.86). Incidence varied across the 47 prefectures (pre-COVID range: 5.0-16.7 per 100,000), and all declined in FY2020 (mean ratio 0.69). Monthly counts peaked in spring-early summer and were higher in spring than in winter (p = 0.018).
CONCLUSIONS: The incidence of surgically treated ATR in Japan was stable before the COVID-19 pandemic, declined markedly in FY2020 and partially recovered thereafter, with the largest reductions among working-age adults and women. Regional variation and seasonality were preserved. These findings can inform surgical and rehabilitation service planning.

title: Sleep Management in Paralympic Sports: Knowledge, Monitoring Practices, and Perceived Barriers among Coaches and Healthcare Staff.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Coaches and healthcare staff play a crucial role in disseminating knowledge about the importance of sleep to develop a precise balance between recovery and the demands imposed by sports training.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the knowledge on sleep, jet lag, and sleep hygiene (SH) among coaches and healthcare staff in Paralympic sports; 2) to identify whether the sleep of Paralympic athletes is monitored, and which instruments are commonly used; and 3) to identify the main barriers faced in sleep management.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The present cross-sectional study was conducted with 60 coaches and healthcare staff who work in the preparation of elite Paralympic athletes. The participants filled out the Sleep Beliefs Scale and a structured questionnaire before traveling to the 2020 Tokyo Paralympic Games.
RESULTS: Coaches and healthcare staff understand the importance of sleep for sports performance and recovery, but only 56% monitored their sleep. The most commonly used methods were subjective. Lack of adherence and commitment among Paralympic athletes (27%) and lack of training (19%) were the main barriers to sleep management.
CONCLUSION: Coaches and healthcare staff are aware of the importance of sleep; however, educational programs are needed to improve the training of coaching and healthcare staff for efficient sleep management and to raise awareness among Paralympic athletes about the importance of sleep.

title: Age-related slowing of sensorimotor reaction time in masters track and field athletes.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Masters athletes offer a powerful model for understanding how lifelong training shapes age‑related changes in reaction time (RT), a key indicator of sensorimotor performance.
PURPOSE: This cross-sectional study examined RT in masters track and field athletes across age, sex, RT tasks of varying complexity, and event disciplines (endurance, power, sprint).
METHODS: A total of 182 competitors (82 females) from the 2025 World Masters Athletics Championships completed four RT tasks using a wireless light-based testing system.
RESULTS: RT increased progressively with age across all tasks, with the slowest responses consistently observed in athletes ≥80 years old. Female athletes demonstrated slower RT than males, and RT increased systematically with task complexity. Sprint athletes showed faster RT than endurance athletes overall, although event‑specific differences did not persist within age groups. Age was positively associated with RT in all tasks (r = 0.41-0.53), with similar correlation strengths between sexes. Quadratic age effects emerged selectively in male athletes for two-hand simple and step-choice tasks, suggesting accelerated slowing at older ages in tasks requiring greater motor coordination. Linear regression models indicated that RT increased by approximately 3.3-3.6 ms per year of age after adjusting for sex, task, and event discipline, while body composition variables were not significant predictors.
CONCLUSIONS: Although lifelong training is associated with better sensorimotor performance, slower RT remains evident in masters athletes, with consistent sex differences and minimal influence of event discipline.

title: Electrospun scaffolds for MSC-derived secretome delivery.
abstract: The mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC)-derived secretome is emerging as a promising cell-free therapeutic product for tissue repair and regeneration. It contains soluble proteins, growth factors, nucleic acids, and extracellular vesicles (EVs), whose combined activity supports angiogenesis, immunomodulation, cytoprotection, and extracellular matrix remodelling. However, the biological activity of these components can be compromised during processing, storage, scaffold loading, and release. This review examines electrospun scaffolds as delivery platforms for the MSC-derived secretome, with particular attention to EV preservation and analytical evaluation. Selected non-electrospun platforms are discussed as comparators to clarify the advantages and limitations of electrospun delivery systems. We discuss how polymer composition, solvent exposure, crosslinking, fibre architecture, and loading strategy affect cargo retention, release kinetics, and biological activity. Post-fabrication adsorption generally minimises processing-related exposure of labile components but often results in rapid release, whereas matrix incorporation, affinity-based immobilisation, and microsphere-assisted loading can prolong delivery while introducing additional risks to vesicle and protein stability. Preclinical studies across these scaffold platforms report beneficial effects in models of skin, bone, cartilage, nerve, periodontal, and cardiac repair, but comparisons remain limited by inconsistent secretome preparation, dose reporting, and analytical methods. Progress towards translation will require standardised characterisation of both soluble and vesicular fractions, dose normalisation to scaffold mass or area, functional potency assays, and validation in long-term, clinically relevant animal models. Together, these developments will enable more reproducible engineering of electrospun secretome-delivery systems and support their clinical translation.

title: Enhancing Sleep in NCAA Division I Athletes: A Study of Sleep Extension Feasibility.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep extension has been shown to improve varied aspects of athletic performance in collegiate athletes. Such studies have been conducted in small cohorts in controlled settings utilizing obsolete monitoring technology. The feasibility of sleep extension has not been evaluated in a broader cohort of collegiate athletes with modern monitoring technology.
HYPOTHESIS: Sleep extension may not be feasible in National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) Division I athletes.
STUDY DESIGN: Crossover study.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 3.
METHODS: Baseline sleep data were collected from NCAA Division I athletes (women's soccer, men's soccer, baseball, and football) during a 2-week period. Subjects were then instructed to extend their total sleep time to 10 hours per night for 2 weeks. All sleep baseline and extension data were collected in the offseason, remote from school examinations. WHOOP bands recorded all sleep metrics. Data were analyzed using paired-samples t tests and Wilcoxon signed rank tests.
RESULTS: A total of 50 subjects (14 female, 36 male) participated. The study compared total sleep time (hours) and sleep consistency (percent) - the stability of sleep-wake schedule over time, between baseline and sleep extension phases. Sample size varied for both metrics, ranging from 46 to 49 participants, respectively. There was a statistically significant increase in sleep consistency during the sleep extension phase (baseline, 60.09 ± 12.6%; extension, 64.42 ± 12.4%; P = 0.02). However, total sleep time showed no significant difference between the 2 phases (baseline, 7.63 ± 0.88 hours; extension, 7.51 ± 0.88 hours; P = 0.27).
CONCLUSION: Extension efforts improved sleep consistency but did not significantly impact total sleep time suggesting that a sleep extension intervention can enhance sleep consistency in NCAA Division I athletes but does not significantly impact total sleep time. Sleep extension may be challenging for collegiate athletes given the time-intensive demands of both academics and sports. While sleep extension may be feasible in professional sports, it does not appear to be so in the college setting.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: While the sleep extension intervention improved sleep consistency, it did not improve total sleep time, questioning the feasibility of sleep extension in collegiate sports.

title: Smartphone Accelerometer Assessment of HRV: Concurrent Agreement of the KubiosHRV App.
abstract: Heart rate variability (HRV) is widely used to monitor athlete recovery and adaptation. Recent technological advances have enabled HRV assessment through smartphone applications without the need for external devices. This study aimed to assess the concurrent agreement between the accelerometer-based HRV measurement feature of the KubiosHRV app and the Polar H10 in supine, seated, and standing positions. A total of 52 participants (30 males and 22 females) across performance tiers 0-4 completed a 2 min resting recording, with the first minute discarded and the second minute analysed in each position. HRV was measured simultaneously using a Polar H10 chest strap and the accelerometer-based feature of the KubiosHRV app on an iPhone 14. The analysed variables included Mean RR, RMSSD, SDNN, LF power, HF power, SD1, and SD2. Data were automatically processed by the KubiosHRV app and manually extracted into a database. Results showed excellent intraclass correlation coefficients (≥0.985) and small magnitudes of error for time-domains and non-linear variables in the three analysed positions with the reference criterion. Frequency-domain variables showed larger error estimates. Bland-Altman analysis showed no evidence of proportional bias across the measurement range (p > 0.05). These findings suggest that, during 1 min recordings, the accelerometer-based feature of the KubiosHRV app showed strong concurrent agreement with the Polar H10 for time-domain variables and acceptable agreement for selected non-linear variables across positions. Therefore, it may represent a practical alternative for routine monitoring of these HRV metrics when external hardware is unavailable.

title: Clinical Considerations With GLP-1 Therapies for Obesity and Knee Osteoarthritis: A Focus on Musculoskeletal Health and Nutritional Concerns.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) therapies and other incretin mimetics represent an important advance in obesity management that could potentially alter the trajectory of knee osteoarthritis (OA) incidence and management approaches. However, enthusiasm should be balanced by awareness about inadvertent musculoskeletal consequences and nutritional considerations.
DESIGN AND RESULTS: This narrative review explores evidence on implications of weight loss on muscle and bone health and malnutrition risk in the context of knee OA. Relevant literature was identified through targeted PubMed searches with emphasis on research gaps and clinical uncertainties. We examine clinical considerations for patient-centered GLP-1 therapy use and recommendations for strategies to optimize nutrition and musculoskeletal health alongside GLP-1 therapies for knee OA management.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The success of GLP-1 therapy use in knee OA management should be evaluated not by the magnitude of weight loss but by improvements in OA symptoms, physical function, body composition, musculoskeletal and cardiometabolic health, and quality of life. Optimizing outcomes will require combining pharmacotherapy with evidence-based nutrition, exercise, and long-term obesity management strategies. Further research is needed to understand how GLP-1 therapies specifically impact musculoskeletal health with knee OA, and best fit into integrated and sustainable strategies for improving joint health.

title: The 'Lower-Trap-Door' technique: Inlay trapezoidal Achilles bone-block fixation for lower trapezius tendon transfer.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe a novel inlay bone-to-bone fixation technique for lower trapezius tendon (LTT) transfer using a trapezoidal humeral osteotomy and Achilles tendon-bone allograft.
METHODS: The Lower-Trap-Door technique incorporates a wedge-shaped calcaneal bone block into a hinged trapezoidal osteotomy at the greater tuberosity. The bone block is press-fitted within the osteotomy and secured using double-row suture anchor fixation. The design creates intrinsic mechanical stability through bone-to-bone contact prior to suture compression. The technique allows integration with superior capsular reconstruction (SCR) when indicated.
RESULTS: This Technical Note details the indications, surgical setup, graft preparation, humeral osteotomy, bone-block insertion, double-row fixation, optional integration with SCR, postoperative rehabilitation, technical pearls, and potential complications. The technique has been used by the senior author in more than 15 patients, with no observed failures at the humeral bone-block interface to date. Formal clinical outcome data are not presented.
CONCLUSION: The Lower-Trap-Door technique provides an inlay bone-to-bone fixation method for LTT transfer using a trapezoidal humeral osteotomy and Achilles tendon-bone allograft. Early clinical use suggests feasibility and construct reliability at the bone-block interface, although formal biomechanical testing and prospective clinical outcome studies are required to validate its comparative effectiveness.

title: Mechanisms and Movement Patterns of Ankle Sprain Injuries in Male Handball: A Video-Based Analysis.
abstract: Ankle sprains are among the most common injuries in handball. However, evidence on high-risk movements and injury circumstances is scarce. This video analysis study investigated the situational characteristics of athletes sustaining ankle sprains. A systematic web search (YouTube, Google News) identifying video recordings of ankle injuries in male handball players was performed. Two independent examiners extracted sample information (e.g., age, height, weight, position), mechanism of injury (direct, indirect, non-contact), movement pattern (landing, change of direction/CoD, running, shuffle, step/lunge, other), action speed, focus of visual attention, and time of injury. In addition to descriptive statistics, χ2-tests were used to examine variable associations. A total of 118 video-recorded injuries were obtained. Most sprains were direct contact injuries (n = 72, 61.0%), and the most frequent movement patterns were landing (n = 46), running (n = 15), step/lunge (n = 14), and CoD (n = 13). While direct injuries occurred primarily during landing (43%), non-contact mechanisms (85%) were, by far, the main cause of injury during change of Direction movements (p < 0.01). In the majority of cases, movement speed was moderate (n = 63) and visual attention was directed to the ball (n = 56). Landings are the most frequent cause of ankle sprains in male handball players. Although the largest share, particularly landing-related injuries, results from direct contact, non-contact sprains display a unique pattern as they mostly occur during CoD. Conditioning coaches and health personnel may consider this disparity when designing preventive measures.

title: Excessive COX-Prostaglandin Signaling Promotes Cellular Senescence and Impaired Skeletal Muscle Recovery in Aging.
abstract: The ability to recover skeletal muscle after periods of disuse declines with age leading to persistent deficits in strength and function that extend beyond muscle mass loss. Here, we investigated whether age-related alterations in lipid remodeling contribute to impairment in skeletal muscle recovery following disuse. Lipidomic and oxylipin profiling revealed that aged mouse muscle is characterized by sustained phosphatidylcholine and omega-6-dependent COX-prostaglandin signaling during early recovery from disuse atrophy. This persistent lipid mediator response was associated with increased senescence burden, fibrosis, and impaired functional recovery. Pharmacological suppression of COX signaling during reloading in aged mice reduced senescence markers, limited fibrosis, and improved muscle function independent of improved muscle size. Mechanistically, senescent induced macrophages produced COX-2-dependent PGE2 and impaired myotube size and fusion through paracrine signaling. Activation of EP2 signaling was sufficient to induce a senescent macrophage phenotype. Importantly, a similar age-associated dysregulation of oxylipin content was observed in older adults after limb immobilization, supporting the translational relevance of these findings. Together, our results identify sustained COX-prostaglandin signaling as a key feature of impaired skeletal muscle recovery with aging and suggest that targeted modulation of this pathway may improve muscle recovery in older individuals. title: Effects of Resveratrol Supplementation on Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) is a common consequence of high-intensity or unfamiliar physical activity and can lead to muscle soreness, inflammation, oxidative stress, and temporary loss of muscle function. Although various interventions have been explored to alleviate EIMD, resveratrol (RES), a natural polyphenolic compound found in grapes, berries, and other plants, has attracted attention due to its potential antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. This review aims to explore the effects of RES on EIMD in terms of its impact on muscle recovery, inflammation, and oxidative stress markers. This review synthesizes the results of preclinical and clinical studies and highlights the timing, dosage, and efficacy of exercise-associated RES. Although the results are promising, with several studies reporting reduced muscle damage and improved recovery, inconsistencies in RES administration timing, dosage, and bioavailability require further investigation. Understanding these factors is critical to optimizing the therapeutic potential of RES in both the exercise and clinical settings. Finally, the review summarizes the potential of RES as a safe and effective intervention for EIMD and implications for future research.

title: Beyond movement behaviours: Unravelling the prospective links between 24-hour behavioural composition and affective dynamics in adolescent athletes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: While the full spectrum of 24-h movement behaviours - encompassing sleep (SLP), screen-based sedentary behaviour (Screen-SB), light physical activity (LPA), structured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (S-MVPA), and unstructured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (US-MVPA) - is consistently linked to daily affective states in adolescent athletes, existing literature has rarely examined these behaviours as an interdependent time-use composition, and largely fails to disentangle the distinct effects of structured versus unstructured MVPA subdomains on emotional outcomes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using a repeated-measures prospective daily design, this study included 161 adolescent athletes (101 males and 60 females). Accelerometers were used to quantify 24-h movement behaviours. Four affective dimensions were assessed through ecological momentary assessment (EMA): high-arousal positive affect, low-arousal positive affect, high-arousal negative affect, and low-arousal negative affect. Bayesian multilevel compositional models were used to estimate between- and within-person associations, while isotemporal substitution analyses evaluated the estimated effects of reallocating time between behaviours on next-day affect.
RESULTS: Associations between 24-h behaviour compositions and next-day affect were more evident at the within-person level. A higher relative proportion of LPA was associated with higher high-arousal positive affect (0.305, 95% Bayesian credible interval [CrI] 0.255 to 0.354) and low-arousal positive affect (0.292, 95% CrI 0.245 to 0.338), and lower high-arousal negative affect (-0.231, 95% CrI -0.260 to -0.203) and low-arousal negative affect (-0.210, 95% CrI -0.236 to -0.185). In 30-min substitution analyses, reallocating time from other behaviours to LPA generally showed more favourable associations with next-day affect at both between- and within-person levels, although the associations varied across substitution pairs and affective dimensions. These findings highlight LPA as the behaviour most consistently associated with favourable next-day affect.
CONCLUSIONS: Daily 24-h movement behaviour composition was prospectively associated with next-day affect in adolescent athletes. LPA showed the most consistent favourable associations with next-day affect, particularly when replacing SB. Promoting LPA may represent a feasible strategy for supporting affective wellbeing without adding to existing training demands.

title: Prevalence and associated factors of depression, anxiety, and stress among university athletes in Bangladesh.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: University athletes face substantial academic, physical, and psychosocial pressures that may heighten vulnerability to psychological distress, despite the perceived mental health benefits of sports participation. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of depression, anxiety, and stress among university athletes in Bangladesh and to examine how these conditions are associated with lifestyle and sociodemographic factors.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted from March to September 2025 among 249 university athletes aged 18-26 years at six randomly selected universities in Bangladesh. Data were collected online and in person. Psychological distress was assessed with the Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21), and health-promoting lifestyle behaviors were evaluated with the Health-Promoting Lifestyle Profile II (HPLP-II). Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, Spearman's correlations, and binary logistic regression analyses were conducted.
RESULTS: The prevalence of depression, anxiety, and stress was 42.6%, 42.6%, and 43.8%, respectively. Depression, anxiety, and stress were significantly associated with relationship status, fatigue, socioeconomic status, smoking, sleep duration, sports participation frequency, and satisfaction with sports (all p < 0.05). Participants with depression, anxiety, and stress had significantly lower scores across all HPLP-II domains (all p < 0.01). Higher physical activity was independently associated with lower odds of depression (OR = 0.462, 95% CI: 0.286-0.746), anxiety (OR = 0.756, 95% CI: 0.677-0.845), and stress (OR = 0.773, 95% CI: 0.677-0.882). Better stress management and stronger interpersonal relationships were also significantly associated, whereas other factors were not.
CONCLUSIONS: Depression, anxiety, and stress were highly prevalent among university athletes in Bangladesh and strongly associated with modifiable lifestyle factors. These findings support integrated, athlete-centered mental health strategies emphasizing physical activity, stress management, and psychosocial support. However, the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference and determination of the directionality of these associations.
